adaptation: SHARED_TOOLS is $SKILL_ROOT/shared, not e2e_workflow/scripts: the shared helpers the skill copies into tasks are bundled at the main revision so this slot does not depend on the e2e_workflow/scripts copies other stages use.
gpu_lock.sh, workspace_sources.py and schema.mjs bundled beside the helpers; gpu_lock_set.py and the skill scripts resolve them as siblings.
delivery_contract.mjs is the five-block extraction of e2e_workflow.js that loadContract() performs, frozen; loadContract(path) still re-extracts from a given checkout.
Tests that drive the GEAK workflow runtime or agentx_kernel_preparation.mjs are dropped; the remaining tests resolve the bundled layout.
references/workflow-handoff.md (GEAK e2e invocation) replaced by references/pipeline-handoff.md (this pipeline's profile slot).

ut_contracts/ (added on this branch): per-operator UT contract families, the contract library and float64 references, the generic gate driver and the task scaffold; SKILL.md §3/§4 and references/task-authoring.md point task authoring at them.

Profile fast path (added on this branch): run_points.py drives every sampling point through one probe server with background per-point censuses (point_census.py, generalized from the per-run census scripts of two GLM-5.2 runs), then coverage_ledger -> build_ranking.py -> select_targets; trace_scan.py replaces json.load for traces; serving_probe.py verifies one rank, closes on settled trace files, aborts and drains its requests and fails graph-hidden decode windows; coverage_ledger divides per_rank censuses by instances; parse_profile knows sglang 0.5.20's VERIFY/DRAFT_EXTEND step names.

Profile template (added on this branch): the agent writes only serving.json (probe_server.py owns the server, keeps decode under --enable-profile-cuda-graph with an eager fallback) and reviews task_decls.json (drafted by draft_task_decls.py from kernel_shapes/source_map/adjacency evidence). relabel_points, plan_ut_cases and build_task_plan.py (lint + task_plan.json + requested_kernel + scaffold_ut) are generalized from the per-run scripts of the 2026-10-20 GLM-5.2 run; families gained `match` patterns; serving_probe arms record_shapes/with_stack, reads realtime_tokens_total for steady state and splits/warms prefill batches before arming (GEAK e82bb297).

Server evidence (added on this branch): probe_server.py records every Triton compile variant and the entry call that built it from process start, warmup and graph capture included (shared/compile_watch.py via a chaining sitecustomize overlay); build_task_plan.py slices it per task; leg_runner.py imports meta.server_preimports first, can record the variants it compiles and replays the recorded calls (--mode server_calls); ut_driver.py adds the server_calls and compile_variants gates. Prompted by Muse Spark attention_2d_prefill/2d_decode passing their UTs and failing in the server (a warmup-only max_seqlen_q=1 variant; sglang's triton.next_power_of_2 rebinding).

Parallel UT wave (added on this branch): scripts/ut_wave.py runs one runner-contract agent lane per task over the deployment's GPUs (docker: one container per lane with only its render nodes), costliest task first, spare GPUs to the costliest tasks, multi-GPU tasks after the single-GPU ones, timing as a tail with every GPU per task; references/ut-lane.md is the lane procedure. harness_lib.measure_legs takes gpus (buckets spread, each bucket's pairs on one device) and _run_leg env_extra/sigs; leg_runner --sigs shards oracle cases and filters server calls; ut_driver shards oracle legs by case, runs server_calls legs side by side, and adds --quick and --reuse.

Multi-config UT (added on this branch): an InferenceX workload is several configs (search-space points), so one task's UT can pool cases from several of them. plan_ut_cases.py plans each config on its own points and phase_summary when the points file carries `configs` (written by the slot's multi_config.py merge) and tags every case with config_id; build_task_plan.manifest prefixes such sigs with '<config_id>/'; scaffold_ut.workload_cases and the ut_contract meta/manifest check carry config_id; harness_lib.serving_weighted_speedup pools the configs per serving_weight_model.config_weighting: `calls` (default; each config's call distribution normalized to 1 and averaged, w(M)=sum_c alpha_c*freq_c(M), the weighting of the 2026-11-02 Muse Spark c8+c32 merge) or `time` (each config's baseline-time mass normalized to alpha_c); alpha equal unless serving_weight_model.config_weights; reports per_config. Cases without config_id take the unchanged single-config path.

Server calls without bulk payload (added on this branch; /shared_nfs/yueliu14/muse_merge_1102/UT_INPUTS_NO_PT_GUIDE.md): compile_watch stores the contents of structural tensors only (index-named, or integer and at most COMPILE_WATCH_STRUCT_CAP = 4 MiB: routing ids, lengths, slots, page tables, small scales). Bulk payloads -- float operands and large integer ones such as packed MXFP4 expert weights and their e8m0 scales -- keep a descriptor plus an evenly spaced sample of COMPILE_WATCH_SAMPLE values: integers are resampled from it on replay (value distribution kept, no NaN exponents), floats drawn from N(mean, std) of it (records without `gen` replay as N(0, 1), as before). One Muse Spark MoE task had stored 0.86 GB a call, 185 GB in all. build_task_plan.server_evidence references a recorded call larger than SERVER_CALL_COPY_MAX (256 MiB) in place by absolute path instead of copying it into the task, so retain/materialize never duplicate it. Recorded calls travel inline: the hook packs a call's structural tensors and samples into the event JSON (tensors_b64) up to COMPILE_WATCH_INLINE_CAP (16 MiB serialized); collect and build_task_plan carry it into run/server_calls.json and leg_runner decodes it (compile_watch.call_data, weights_only) -- so a task directory holds no tensor file. calls/*.pt is written only above the cap.

Live-run fixes (added on this branch, made by the profile agent of the 2026-11-02 Muse Spark campaign on crsuse2-m2m-100, reviewed): source_map.py maps the absolute frame paths of an editable install (/sgl-workspace/sglang/python/sglang/...) to the package-relative form, without which every frame of the image's editable sglang was dropped and its kernels had no operator; ut_wave.py accepts UT_WAVE_ORDER (explicit task priority), UT_WAVE_CONTAINER_PREFIX (campaign container naming) and UT_WAVE_DOCKER_EXTRA (extra mounts, never device options), all defaulting to the previous behaviour; compile_watch._sample builds gather positions in float64 clamped to the span (a float32 linspace over > 2**24 elements indexed past the storage and faulted the GPU) and never samples inside graph capture.

server_calls postprocess hook (added on this branch, 2026-11-04): meta.ut_contract.server_call_postprocess lets a task reduce the replayed return in BOTH legs through cases.server_call_postprocess(call, args, kwargs, ret) before compare_call_outputs. leg_runner._server_calls invokes the resolved entry directly, so cases.call() does not run; an entry whose return is only partly defined -- a routed MoE expert kernel allocates its output with torch.empty and writes only the rows that land on this rank, and the deployed caller masks the rest by the same routing and never reads them -- then had its uninitialized region compared, which two identical calls of the UNMODIFIED entry do not even match (Muse Spark EP4, op__compact_a4_experts: 168 of 260 replayed calls failed on out.return with nan_match false in both legs). The hook is frozen task source outside the candidate overlay, so it reduces both legs identically; ut_driver reports it and its stated why in the gate result. shared/leg_runner.py and ut_contracts/{ut_driver.py,README.md}.

decode on the eager server (added on this branch, 2026-11-05): with --server-state decode_capture=profile_cuda_graph, run_points.py captures PREFILL only and marks every DECODE point deferred (graph_hidden, no capture); probe_server.py restarts eagerly and redoes exactly those. Under spec decoding the profiler kept 1 of 8 VERIFY graph replays on most ranks (sglang 0.5.21 / ROCm 7.2), so every decode point of the Muse Spark EP4 group was refused and recaptured eagerly after a failed attempt each. --decode-on-graph restores the old order.

merge_policy.py (added on this branch, 2026-11-05): decides which tasks of a multi-config group are one UT. Same launch group + same entry pools every config; a launch_diff setting splits a task only if its own source reads it; entries chosen above them by batch size (one common caller, different call lines, each under a conditional, never launched at one sampled point, non-interleaving sizes) are ONE task, merged as dispatcher / rebuilt_instance / scope_equalized by what the seam's recorded arguments allow. The reviewer had split aiter_backend._muse_verify_attention's branches on the wrong premise that it takes a ForwardBatch.

compile_watch.literal_object (2026-11-05): a recorded builtin container of literals (frozenset/set/dict/tuple, repr not truncated) is a replayable value; plan_call used to refuse _muse_verify_attention for its enabled-kernel frozenset.

harness_lib.serving_weighted_speedup per_branch / worst_branch (2026-11-05): when cases carry `branch` (a merged branch group), one figure per branch, so a gain on one branch cannot hide a loss on another.
